provision.text: Discrepancy Notices. Discrepancy notices are written requests from board members for clarification or amplification of information found in an officer's OMPF. The Commandant of the Marine Corps (MMRP) is the sole agency authorized to furnish information related to discrepancy notices. The CMC (MMPR-1) is responsible for ensuring all information requested by or furnished to a promotion board is in compliance with sections 614 and 14107 of reference (a), reference (d) and reference (q) and 1412.9B. In addition, the following guidance will be adhered to:
Board members are the only individuals authorized to submit discrepancy notices.
Discrepancy notices can only be answered if they pertain to information included in an officer's OMPF per MCO P1070.12K.
Any discrepancy notice that requests information not found in an officer's OMPF cannot be lawfully answered or furnished to the selection board.
The selection board president, members, recorders, and MMPR-1 personnel are prohibited from contacting officers or commands relating to discrepancy notices.
Information furnished to the board must refer to performance or actions that occurred prior to the convening date of the board.

provision.text: Remove. An officer whose name is removed from a promotion list per section 629 of reference (a) incurs a failure of selection (unless selected from the below zone) and continues to be eligible for consideration for promotion. If the officer is recommended for promotion by the next selection board, and the SECNAV approves the report of the board, the officer's name shall be placed on the promotion list without prejudice. Per sections 629 and 14501 of reference (a), an officer once removed is considered for all purposes as having twice failed of selection for promotion to the next higher grade upon the following: the officer is not recommended for promotion in the approved report of the next selection board; the officer is so recommended, but the President, or the SECNAV acting for the President, removes the officer's name from the promotion list; or if the Senate rejects the officer's appointment. 5004. BOARD REPORT. Upon completion of deliberations, the CMC (MMPR-1), in accordance with reference (d), will prepare a selection board report. The board report contains a list of all selectees and the following administrative documents as specified in the precept: statistical analysis, precept, a list of the officers eligible for consideration for promotion, officers selected for merit reorder; notice of convening, promotion plan, and sampling of records. The board report must be signed and certified by each board member and recorder. Board reports will be maintained per SECNAV-M 5210.1 record schedule 1000-13. 4001. UNAUTHORIZED RELEASE OF BOARD PROCEEDINGS. Reference (a), reference (d), and reference (q) prohibit the disclosure of the proceedings of selection boards to any person not a member or recorder of a board. In addition, reference (q) further states that no member or recorder of a selection board may counsel officers who failed of selection by that board. Board presidents are charged to brief the members and recorders of the board, both upon convening and immediately prior to adjournment, that proceedings, deliberations, materials, and any other information pertaining to the board are not releasable except as authorized by the SECNAV, the Secretary of Defense, or the President. Officer counseling and evaluation, CMC (MMRP-50), for both active duty and reserve officers, may counsel officers who fail of selection boards. Reserve officers may contact Reserve Affairs and receive counseling and evaluations from the Career Management Team (CMT). 4002. FAILURE OF SELECTION

PROMOTION BOARD SCHEDULE. Officer promotion boards are based on a fiscal year schedule. In the second quarter of each fiscal year, the CMC (MMPR-1) will publish the board schedule, via MARADMIN, for the succeeding fiscal year. In addition to the board convening dates, this message will contain information on reviewing and updating an officer’s Official Military Personnel File (OMPF) and other administrative instructions that are applicable to all promotion boards. 2001. Sections 614 and 14105 of reference (a) require that, at least 30 days prior to the date the board is convened, the CMC (MMPR- 1) must provide general written notice to eligible officers. This shall be accomplished through a standard naval message (MARADMIN), and at a minimum will include:

provision.text: Any information regarding an action that was completed after the date the board convened (e.g. awards certificates, fitness reports, disciplinary actions, etc.). 3002. REQUEST FOR NON-SELECTION. Some eligible officers on the active-duty list may intend to leave active duty and therefore submit a written request not to be selected for promotion to the board president. Any officer In or Above-Zone who submits a request for non-selection will still be considered by the board, but will incur a failure of selection if not recommended for promotion by the board. Per section 1174 of reference (a), an officer discharged for twice failing of selection is not entitled to separation pay if either (or both) of those failures of selection was the action of a selection board to which the officer submitted a request in writing not to be selected for promotion or who otherwise directly caused his/her own non-selection through written communication to the board. Accordingly, selection boards convened under sections 611a of reference (a) are required to include in the board report the names of those officers who fall into this category. All requests for non-selection must be received within ten calendar days of the board convene date per 10 U.S.C. section 614. 3003. RESERVE QUALIFICATION SUMMARY (RQS). Reserve officers (except AR officers) are required to submit an RQS to selection boards for which they are eligible. This document provides valuable information regarding the officer's activities when not actively participating in the Reserve Marine Corps. Additional information pertaining to the RQS requirement is outlined in the annual Board Schedule MARADMIN. 3004. ASSIGNMENT OF CASES. Assignment of eligible officers' cases to each board member is accomplished randomly by computer amongst the board members. Board presidents will be assigned half the number of cases as other board members to account for the additional administrative duties associated with their position. 3005. CASE PREPARATION AND BRIEFING. The officer selection process is composed of four phases, thus ensuring each officer's record is thoroughly reviewed, briefed, considered, and voted on by the selection board.

provision.text: Limited Duty Officer (LDO). All Limited Duty Officers (LDO) secure appointments as a regular officer in the Marine Corps for the performance of duty in the technical field in which they are proficient. These officers are technically oriented, perform duties that are limited to specific occupational fields, and do not have the normal career pattern of unrestricted officers. Per SECNAVINST 1412.11, LDOs compete within their military occupational specialty (MOS) among other LDOs of the same grade for promotions to major and lieutenant colonel via selection boards. There are no LDOs in the Marine Corps Reserve.

provision.text: In-Zone (Promotion Zone). In-Zone officers have neither failed of selection for promotion nor been removed from a promotion list. In-Zone officers comprise the primary eligible population for consideration by the selection board. If not selected, the officer will incur a failure of selection. It is common to have officers whose lineal precedence falls within the Above-Zone population, but who are In-Zone officers (Above-Zone, not previously considered). These officers will be given the same consideration as any other In-Zone case. This zone is determined utilizing the authorized number of officers to select and the selection opportunity.

provision.text: Below-Zone (Below the Promotion Zone). Below-Zone officers are junior to the junior officer in the promotion zone (In-Zone). Below-Zone officers are eligible for consideration, but if not selected, they will not incur a failure of selection. The number of Below-Zone officers authorized to be selected may not exceed 10 percent of the total number of officers the PSB is authorized to recommend for promotion; however, where the number authorized by this calculation would be less than one, the board may recommend one Below- Zone officer. Additionally, the Below-Zone population is generally a rough estimate of the following year's In-Zone population. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 1-11 Enclosure (2)

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Remove. An officer whose name is removed from a promotion list per section 629 of reference (a) incurs a failure of selection (unless selected from the below zone) and continues to be eligible for consideration for promotion. If the officer is recommended for promotion by the next selection board, and the SECNAV approves the report of the board, the officer's name shall be placed on the promotion list without prejudice. Per sections 629 and 14501 of reference (a), an officer once removed is considered for all purposes as having twice failed of selection for promotion to the next higher grade upon the following: the officer is not recommended for promotion in the approved report of the next selection board; the officer is so recommended, but the President, or the SECNAV acting for the President, removes the officer's name from the promotion list; or if the Senate rejects the officer's appointment. 5004. Carry Over. Failures of selection do not carry over between competitive categories (i.e. active duty failures do not carry over to the Reserve component). Once an officer has failed of selection in one competitive category, that failure of selection is maintained in that same competitive category. 4003. SAMPLING OF RECORDS. Per reference (q), the sampling of records is included as part of the administrative documents contained in the board report. Sample select and non-select records are chosen for possible future use at special selection boards and special selection review boards. The record will be maintained as it looked the date the board convened, to include any update material sent by the eligible officer. See Chapter 7 for information on special selection boards and special selection review boards. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 4-3 Enclosure (2) 4004. SHOW CAUSE. As outlined in paragraph 3008, a letter from the board president to Deputy Commandant, Manpower and Reserve Affairs that contains a paragraph detailing the basis for the board’s findings will be forwarded. 4005. ADVERSE SCREENING. An adverse screening is conducted prior to, for General Officer promotion selection boards, and after adjournment for every other promotion board. An adverse screening is also completed prior to the release of each month’s promotion MARADMIN. See Chapter 5 for a complete discussion of the adverse process. 4006. NOMINATION PACKAGE. Senate confirmation is required for all officers on active duty selected for promotion to the grades of major or above, and colonel or above for Reserve boards, before an officer may be promoted or frocked. Approval by the SECDEF or his or her designee is required for active CWOs and Reserve officers selected for promotion to the grades of captain through lieutenant colonel before an officer may be promoted or frocked. Upon completion of the adverse screening, the CMC (MMPR-1) prepares a nomination package for all boards requiring Presidential and Senate approval. Reference

PROMOTION BOARD SCHEDULE. Officer promotion boards are based on a fiscal year schedule. In the second quarter of each fiscal year, the CMC (MMPR-1) will publish the board schedule, via MARADMIN, for the succeeding fiscal year. In addition to the board convening dates, this message will contain information on reviewing and updating an officer’s Official Military Personnel File (OMPF) and other administrative instructions that are applicable to all promotion boards. 2001. NOTICE OF CONVENING. Sections 614 and 14105 of reference (a) require that, at least 30 days prior to the date the board is convened, the CMC (MMPR- 1) must provide general written notice to eligible officers. This shall be accomplished through a standard naval message (MARADMIN), and at a minimum will include:

provision.label: a.
provision.text: The name and date of the junior eligible officer in the below-zone as of the date of the notice.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Submission of update material to the board.

provision.text: Submission of Reserve Qualification Summaries (RQS) to Reserve selection boards.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Implementation of any unique regulation such as the 90-day rule or continuation in an active status. 2002. BOARD COMPOSITION

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Open-source information not contained in the OMPF, such as school and command screening messages. Any information that is not part of an officer's OMPF is strictly prohibited.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Current separation or retirement status, unless provided by the eligible officer as update material sent to the President of the board.

provision.text: Current medical status, unless provided by the eligible officer as update material sent to the President of the board. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 3-4 Enclosure (2)

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Any information received from third parties not endorsed or forwarded by the eligible officer.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Any information regarding an action that was completed after the date the board convened (e.g. awards certificates, fitness reports, disciplinary actions, etc.). 3002. REQUEST FOR NON-SELECTION. Some eligible officers on the active-duty list may intend to leave active duty and therefore submit a written request not to be selected for promotion to the board president. Any officer In or Above-Zone who submits a request for non-selection will still be considered by the board, but will incur a failure of selection if not recommended for promotion by the board. Per section 1174 of reference (a), an officer discharged for twice failing of selection is not entitled to separation pay if either (or both) of those failures of selection was the action of a selection board to which the officer submitted a request in writing not to be selected for promotion or who otherwise directly caused his/her own non-selection through written communication to the board. Accordingly, selection boards convened under sections 611a of reference (a) are required to include in the board report the names of those officers who fall into this category. All requests for non-selection must be received within ten calendar days of the board convene date per 10 U.S.C. section 614. 3003. RESERVE QUALIFICATION SUMMARY (RQS). Reserve officers (except AR officers) are required to submit an RQS to selection boards for which they are eligible. This document provides valuable information regarding the officer's activities when not actively participating in the Reserve Marine Corps. Additional information pertaining to the RQS requirement is outlined in the annual Board Schedule MARADMIN. 3004. ASSIGNMENT OF CASES. Assignment of eligible officers' cases to each board member is accomplished randomly by computer amongst the board members. Board presidents will be assigned half the number of cases as other board members to account for the additional administrative duties associated with their position. 3005. CASE PREPARATION AND BRIEFING. The officer selection process is composed of four phases, thus ensuring each officer's record is thoroughly reviewed, briefed, considered, and voted on by the selection board.

Once the members of a board sign the board report and the CMC (MMPR-1) has prepared the nomination package, both packages are forwarded to the final approval authority. All selection boards must be endorsed, first by the Commandant of the Marine Corps, and second by the Office of the Judge Advocate General of the Navy, before being forwarded to the SECNAV. Figure 4-1 contains a detailed chart, which indicates the offices the board report, and, when applicable, the nomination package must be routed through prior to release of the results and ultimate board approval authority. 4008. NOTIFICATION OF BOARD RESULTS

Advance Notification. The Commandant of the Marine Corps, in keeping with the Marine Corps principle of caring for our own, has established an advance notification system which reduces the insensitiveness of notification through message traffic. This advance notification will be sent only to General Officers and Senior Executive Service (SES), tasked with notifying selected/non-selected officers. It provides leadership options in addressing the obvious disappointment of officers not selected for promotion. General Officers may delegate notification authority to regimental/group and battalion/squadron commanders. For General Officers serving in HQMC or other external staff assignments, notification authority may be delegated to deputies or executive assistants. The advance notification will be in the form of a P4 (personnel for, distribution list) and will be treated as close hold until the selection list ALNAV has been released. The P4 will be sent upon board approval authority action and will contain the following:

INTRODUCTION. The officer promotion process is founded upon the selection and promotion of the best and fully qualified Marines. Selection boards utilize the information authorized by law to be furnished to them in order to determine which Marines meet the best and fully qualified standard; however, potentially adverse information is not always available to promotion boards. Officers who are already selected and nominated but not yet promoted may commit acts that call into question their suitability for promotion. In order to ensure officers to be promoted meet the highest standards of conduct, the CMC (MMPR-1), in coordination with the Staff Judge Advocate to the Commandant of the Marine Corps (SJA to CMC), manages the officer promotion adverse process. 5001. ADVERSE INFORMATION AVAILABLE TO PROMOTION BOARDS. Reference (a) and reference (d) give specific guidance on how promotion selection boards must treat adverse (or potentially adverse) information. If adverse information appears in information authorized to be furnished to a promotion board, that information must be briefed to the board. This information can be briefed because, by virtue of its appearance in the officer’s record, the officer has had the opportunity to respond to that information. Information of an adverse nature not contained in the officer’s record cannot be briefed because the officer has not had the opportunity to respond to that information. 5002. ADVERSE SCREENING AND SPECIAL SELECTION REVIEW BOARDS (SSRB). Section 505 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2021, added sections 628a and 14502a to reference (a) that requires the Secretary of the Military Department concerned to convene a SSRB to consider credible information of an adverse nature, including any substantiated adverse finding or conclusion, that was not furnished to a PSB convened under reference (a) sections 611(a) and 14101(a). Additionally, the Office of the SECDEF requires a “robust adverse review” off all officer promotion boards, not just boards where officers are confirmed by the Senate. Any SSRB convened, whether for a regular or reserve officer, to a grade at or below the grade of major general, would, to the greatest extent practicable, apply the same standards used by the PSB that originally recommended the officer for promotion and would consider the record of the officer as presented to the original PSB, along with the newly adjudicated adverse information. The SSRB will be conducted so as not to indicate or disclose the officer, or officers, for whom the board is convened, as statute prohibits any affirmative action to label/identify the record for whom the SSRB is convened. The members of the SSRB are to apply a competitive process to determine whether or not to sustain the original promotion recommendation of the officer(s) at issue. An officer whose promotion is recommended for sustainment by a SSRB would be appointed, pending the review and confirmation process, to the next higher grade, as soon as the Record of Proceedings (ROP) is approved, and, upon appointment, would have the same date of rank as the officer would have had pursuant to the recommendation of the original PSB. If a SSRB does not sustain a recommendation for promotion of an officer, that officer will be considered to have failed selection for promotion. 5003. POST-BOARD SCREENING/WITHHOLD PROCESS. Upon adjournment of a promotion selection board, a review of investigative files is conducted to determine if any of the selected officers have potentially adverse information. If this review uncovers such information, the officer will be reviewed for withholding from nomination. The Staff Judge Advocate to the Commandant (SJA to CMC) conducts the review of the potentially adverse information and provides information to the Commandant of the Marine Corps. Based on the individual MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 5-3 Enclosure (2) case, the Commandant of the Marine Corps will make a recommendation to the SECNAV on whether to support the officer’s nomination, or to recommend withholding the officer’s name pending further review. If the decision is to nominate, the officer’s name remains in the nomination package and on the ALNAV. If not, the officer is withheld and notice and comment procedures are initiated when the board results are released.

provision.text: Limited Duty Officer (LDO). All Limited Duty Officers (LDO) secure appointments as a regular officer in the Marine Corps for the performance of duty in the technical field in which they are proficient. These officers are technically oriented, perform duties that are limited to specific occupational fields, and do not have the normal career pattern of unrestricted officers. Per SECNAVINST 1412.11, LDOs compete within their military occupational specialty (MOS) among other LDOs of the same grade for promotions to major and lieutenant colonel via selection boards. There are no LDOs in the Marine Corps Reserve.

provision.text: In-Zone (Promotion Zone). In-Zone officers have neither failed of selection for promotion nor been removed from a promotion list. In-Zone officers comprise the primary eligible population for consideration by the selection board. If not selected, the officer will incur a failure of selection. It is common to have officers whose lineal precedence falls within the Above-Zone population, but who are In-Zone officers (Above-Zone, not previously considered). These officers will be given the same consideration as any other In-Zone case. This zone is determined utilizing the authorized number of officers to select and the selection opportunity.

provision.text: Below-Zone (Below the Promotion Zone). Below-Zone officers are junior to the junior officer in the promotion zone (In-Zone). Below-Zone officers are eligible for consideration, but if not selected, they will not incur a failure of selection. The number of Below-Zone officers authorized to be selected may not exceed 10 percent of the total number of officers the PSB is authorized to recommend for promotion; however, where the number authorized by this calculation would be less than one, the board may recommend one Below- Zone officer. Additionally, the Below-Zone population is generally a rough estimate of the following year's In-Zone population. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 1-11 Enclosure (2)

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Discrepancy Notices. Discrepancy notices are written requests from board members for clarification or amplification of information found in an officer's OMPF. The Commandant of the Marine Corps (MMRP) is the sole agency authorized to furnish information related to discrepancy notices. The CMC (MMPR-1) is responsible for ensuring all information requested by or furnished to a promotion board is in compliance with sections 614 and 14107 of reference (a), reference (d) and reference (q) and 1412.9B. In addition, the following guidance will be adhered to:
Board members are the only individuals authorized to submit discrepancy notices.
Discrepancy notices can only be answered if they pertain to information included in an officer's OMPF per MCO P1070.12K.
Any discrepancy notice that requests information not found in an officer's OMPF cannot be lawfully answered or furnished to the selection board.
The selection board president, members, recorders, and MMPR-1 personnel are prohibited from contacting officers or commands relating to discrepancy notices.
Information furnished to the board must refer to performance or actions that occurred prior to the convening date of the board.

provision.text: Promote. If the decision is that the officer should be promoted, a separate nomination package containing the officer’s name shall be forwarded to the Secretary of Defense (for USMC CWOs and Capts, and USMCR Capts - LtCols), the President or the Senate (for USMC Majs - MajGen and USMCR Col- MajGen), as appropriate. Officers who are nominated after a period of withholding, who have passed the date when they would have been promoted, will receive their original date of rank upon approval, as appropriate, unless the SECNAV determines that the officer was unqualified for promotion for any period of time during the official delay. In such cases the SECNAV may adjust the date of rank to reflect periods of non-qualification.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Remove. An officer whose name is removed from a promotion list per section 629 of reference (a) incurs a failure of selection (unless selected from the below zone) and continues to be eligible for consideration for promotion. If the officer is recommended for promotion by the next selection board, and the SECNAV approves the report of the board, the officer's name shall be placed on the promotion list without prejudice. Per sections 629 and 14501 of reference (a), an officer once removed is considered for all purposes as having twice failed of selection for promotion to the next higher grade upon the following: the officer is not recommended for promotion in the approved report of the next selection board; the officer is so recommended, but the President, or the SECNAV acting for the President, removes the officer's name from the promotion list; or if the Senate rejects the officer's appointment. 5004. Notice and Comment Procedures. If the SECNAV withholds an officer’s name from nomination, the officer shall be notified in writing of such action and be afforded the opportunity to submit a written statement to the SECNAV via the chain of command. If the officer declines to make a statement, the officer shall submit a signed statement to that effect. After a review of the officer's statement, the Commandant of the Marine Corps will recommend either that the officer be promoted, in which case the officer is required to be sent to a SSRB, as discussed in paragraph 5002, or that he/she be removed from the promotion list. Furthermore, an officer may be withheld pending an investigation. If the investigation is unsubstantiated, the Commandant of the Marine Corps may recommend to promote the officer without a SSRB (there is nothing adverse for a SSRB to consider.)

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Limited Duty Officer (LDO). All Limited Duty Officers (LDO) secure appointments as a regular officer in the Marine Corps for the performance of duty in the technical field in which they are proficient. These officers are technically oriented, perform duties that are limited to specific occupational fields, and do not have the normal career pattern of unrestricted officers. Per SECNAVINST 1412.11, LDOs compete within their military occupational specialty (MOS) among other LDOs of the same grade for promotions to major and lieutenant colonel via selection boards. There are no LDOs in the Marine Corps Reserve.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: In-Zone (Promotion Zone). In-Zone officers have neither failed of selection for promotion nor been removed from a promotion list. In-Zone officers comprise the primary eligible population for consideration by the selection board. If not selected, the officer will incur a failure of selection. It is common to have officers whose lineal precedence falls within the Above-Zone population, but who are In-Zone officers (Above-Zone, not previously considered). These officers will be given the same consideration as any other In-Zone case. This zone is determined utilizing the authorized number of officers to select and the selection opportunity.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Below-Zone (Below the Promotion Zone). Below-Zone officers are junior to the junior officer in the promotion zone (In-Zone). Below-Zone officers are eligible for consideration, but if not selected, they will not incur a failure of selection. The number of Below-Zone officers authorized to be selected may not exceed 10 percent of the total number of officers the PSB is authorized to recommend for promotion; however, where the number authorized by this calculation would be less than one, the board may recommend one Below- Zone officer. Additionally, the Below-Zone population is generally a rough estimate of the following year's In-Zone population. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 1-11 Enclosure (2)

Such education or advanced degree is required as a prerequisite for appointment, designation, or assignment as a commissioned officer in a particular professional specialty; and
The officer completes the advanced education or receives the advanced degree in less than the number of years normally required to do so.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: The CMC (MMPR-1), for active duty only, executes the continuation board based on the promotion plan and with the eligible population provided by Separations and Retirement Branch (CMC (MMSR)). CMC (MMPR-1) provides administrative oversight of the nomination package and delivers the results to CMC (MMSR). CMC (MMSR) is responsible for administering the results of continuation boards and will notify officers selected for continuation. An officer who is selected for continuation shall be afforded an opportunity to accept or decline the continuation. Those officers not selected for continuation will be notified by official correspondence from the CMC (MMSR), that they are required to separate no later than the first day of the seventh month, following approval of the board. The separation of an officer who declines continuation will be considered as an involuntary separation under sections 580 and 637 of reference (a), unless the officer voluntarily resigns prior to the involuntary separation date.

Any material received without the officer's endorsement will not be submitted to the board. provision.label: b.
provision.text: Remove. An officer whose name is removed from a promotion list per section 629 of reference (a) incurs a failure of selection (unless selected from the below zone) and continues to be eligible for consideration for promotion. If the officer is recommended for promotion by the next selection board, and the SECNAV approves the report of the board, the officer's name shall be placed on the promotion list without prejudice. Per sections 629 and 14501 of reference (a), an officer once removed is considered for all purposes as having twice failed of selection for promotion to the next higher grade upon the following: the officer is not recommended for promotion in the approved report of the next selection board; the officer is so recommended, but the President, or the SECNAV acting for the President, removes the officer's name from the promotion list; or if the Senate rejects the officer's appointment. 5004. provision.label: a.
provision.text: Limited Duty Officer (LDO). All Limited Duty Officers (LDO) secure appointments as a regular officer in the Marine Corps for the performance of duty in the technical field in which they are proficient. These officers are technically oriented, perform duties that are limited to specific occupational fields, and do not have the normal career pattern of unrestricted officers. Per SECNAVINST 1412.11, LDOs compete within their military occupational specialty (MOS) among other LDOs of the same grade for promotions to major and lieutenant colonel via selection boards. There are no LDOs in the Marine Corps Reserve.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: In-Zone (Promotion Zone). In-Zone officers have neither failed of selection for promotion nor been removed from a promotion list. In-Zone officers comprise the primary eligible population for consideration by the selection board. If not selected, the officer will incur a failure of selection. It is common to have officers whose lineal precedence falls within the Above-Zone population, but who are In-Zone officers (Above-Zone, not previously considered). These officers will be given the same consideration as any other In-Zone case. This zone is determined utilizing the authorized number of officers to select and the selection opportunity.

provision.text: Below-Zone (Below the Promotion Zone). Below-Zone officers are junior to the junior officer in the promotion zone (In-Zone). Below-Zone officers are eligible for consideration, but if not selected, they will not incur a failure of selection. The number of Below-Zone officers authorized to be selected may not exceed 10 percent of the total number of officers the PSB is authorized to recommend for promotion; however, where the number authorized by this calculation would be less than one, the board may recommend one Below- Zone officer. Additionally, the Below-Zone population is generally a rough estimate of the following year's In-Zone population. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 1-11 Enclosure (2)

Such education or advanced degree is required as a prerequisite for appointment, designation, or assignment as a commissioned officer in a particular professional specialty; and
The officer completes the advanced education or receives the advanced degree in less than the number of years normally required to do so.
The amount of constructive service credit that may be awarded to an officer who qualifies for a waiver of this restriction is limited to the difference between:

provision.label: (a)

Once nominated, officers will only be replaced upon approval of the CMC (MM) due to the requirement to seek approval of any precept changes from the SECNAV.

Nominations of officers to serve on selection boards are sensitive in nature; therefore, knowledge of their appointment should be limited to only those individuals who have a need to know. Upon adjournment of the selection board, public dissemination is authorized. 2003. PRECEPT

Commanding Officers must give written notice to an officer outlining the grounds for the delay before the effective date of the appointment (see figure 5-1), unless impracticable to do. If extenuating circumstances exist, written notice shall be given as soon as practicable. This notice must give the officer the opportunity to make a statement.

The command must notify the CMC (MMPR-1) and SJA to CMC of its intent to delay the officer's promotion in writing. This will ensure that an officer's promotion is not effected. The notification shall include a report of the circumstances, a copy of the letter provided to the officer concerned of the intent to delay that officer's promotion, and a written acknowledgment of receipt from the officer (to include his or her decision on submitting a statement). The report of the delay action shall be submitted within 10 days of knowledge of the circumstances warranting the delay.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: The CMC (MMPR-1), for active duty only, executes the continuation board based on the promotion plan and with the eligible population provided by Separations and Retirement Branch (CMC (MMSR)). CMC (MMPR-1) provides administrative oversight of the nomination package and delivers the results to CMC (MMSR). CMC (MMSR) is responsible for administering the results of continuation boards and will notify officers selected for continuation. An officer who is selected for continuation shall be afforded an opportunity to accept or decline the continuation. Those officers not selected for continuation will be notified by official correspondence from the CMC (MMSR), that they are required to separate no later than the first day of the seventh month, following approval of the board. The separation of an officer who declines continuation will be considered as an involuntary separation under sections 580 and 637 of reference (a), unless the officer voluntarily resigns prior to the involuntary separation date.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Discrepancy Notices. Discrepancy notices are written requests from board members for clarification or amplification of information found in an officer's OMPF. The Commandant of the Marine Corps (MMRP) is the sole agency authorized to furnish information related to discrepancy notices. The CMC (MMPR-1) is responsible for ensuring all information requested by or furnished to a promotion board is in compliance with sections 614 and 14107 of reference (a), reference (d) and reference (q) and 1412.9B. In addition, the following guidance will be adhered to:
Board members are the only individuals authorized to submit discrepancy notices.
Discrepancy notices can only be answered if they pertain to information included in an officer's OMPF per MCO P1070.12K.
Any discrepancy notice that requests information not found in an officer's OMPF cannot be lawfully answered or furnished to the selection board.
The selection board president, members, recorders, and MMPR-1 personnel are prohibited from contacting officers or commands relating to discrepancy notices.
Information furnished to the board must refer to performance or actions that occurred prior to the convening date of the board.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Promote. If the decision is that the officer should be promoted, a separate nomination package containing the officer’s name shall be forwarded to the Secretary of Defense (for USMC CWOs and Capts, and USMCR Capts - LtCols), the President or the Senate (for USMC Majs - MajGen and USMCR Col- MajGen), as appropriate. Officers who are nominated after a period of withholding, who have passed the date when they would have been promoted, will receive their original date of rank upon approval, as appropriate, unless the SECNAV determines that the officer was unqualified for promotion for any period of time during the official delay. In such cases the SECNAV may adjust the date of rank to reflect periods of non-qualification.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Remove. An officer whose name is removed from a promotion list per section 629 of reference (a) incurs a failure of selection (unless selected from the below zone) and continues to be eligible for consideration for promotion. If the officer is recommended for promotion by the next selection board, and the SECNAV approves the report of the board, the officer's name shall be placed on the promotion list without prejudice. Per sections 629 and 14501 of reference (a), an officer once removed is considered for all purposes as having twice failed of selection for promotion to the next higher grade upon the following: the officer is not recommended for promotion in the approved report of the next selection board; the officer is so recommended, but the President, or the SECNAV acting for the President, removes the officer's name from the promotion list; or if the Senate rejects the officer's appointment. 5004. MONTHLY SCREENING/DELAY PROCESS

Resolution-Delays

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Promote. If the decision is that the officer should be promoted, the officer will receive the original date of rank he/she would have had if no such delay had occurred; however, per reference (a), sections 624 and 14311, the SECNAV has the authority to adjust the date of rank of an officer if the Secretary believes the officer was unqualified for promotion during any part of the period of delay. For second lieutenants promoted to first lieutenant, and warrant officers promoted to chief warrant officer 2, date of rank adjustment authority rests with the Commandant of the Marine Corps.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Remove. Removal decision actions for promotion delays are the same as for promotion withholds (see paragraph 5003.2.b). 5005. ELIGIBILITY IMPLICATIONS. While an officer is in a withhold or a delay status, he/she is not eligible for any subsequent promotion boards. Sections 619 and 14301 of reference (a) preclude from consideration an officer whose name is on a promotion list for that grade as a result of selection at a previous promotion board (or eligibility for promotion as a result of achieving time in grade requirements). 5006. SPECIAL SELECTION BOARDS (SSBs) AND SPECIAL SELECTION REVIEW BOARDS (SSRBs). Post-board screening for officers selected for promotion by an SSB or SSRB is conducted in accordance with the procedures outlined in paragraph 5002 and 5003. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 5-5 Enclosure (2) 5007. SECOND LIEUTENANTS (O-1). All second lieutenants appointed during a calendar year are screened for qualifications for promotion to first lieutenant and their names are forwarded to the Secretary of Defense for approval prior to appointment to first lieutenant. Officers with adverse material will follow the same procedures listed above with regard to the opportunity to comment and subsequent qualification for promotion decision. 5008. WARRANT OFFICERS (W-1). All W-1s appointed during a calendar year are screened for qualification for promotion to chief warrant officer 2 and their names are forwarded to the Secretary of Defense for approval prior to appointment to chief warrant officer 2 (CWO2). Officers with adverse material will follow the same procedures listed above with regard to the opportunity to comment and subsequent qualification for promotion decision. provision.label: a.
provision.text: Limited Duty Officer (LDO). All Limited Duty Officers (LDO) secure appointments as a regular officer in the Marine Corps for the performance of duty in the technical field in which they are proficient. These officers are technically oriented, perform duties that are limited to specific occupational fields, and do not have the normal career pattern of unrestricted officers. Per SECNAVINST 1412.11, LDOs compete within their military occupational specialty (MOS) among other LDOs of the same grade for promotions to major and lieutenant colonel via selection boards. There are no LDOs in the Marine Corps Reserve.

provision.text: Above-Zone (Above the Promotion Zone). Above-Zone officers have been previously considered in the In-Zone population, and failed selection for promotion by a regularly scheduled board. These officers will incur additional failures of selection if not selected by subsequent selection boards.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: In-Zone (Promotion Zone). In-Zone officers have neither failed of selection for promotion nor been removed from a promotion list. In-Zone officers comprise the primary eligible population for consideration by the selection board. If not selected, the officer will incur a failure of selection. It is common to have officers whose lineal precedence falls within the Above-Zone population, but who are In-Zone officers (Above-Zone, not previously considered). These officers will be given the same consideration as any other In-Zone case. This zone is determined utilizing the authorized number of officers to select and the selection opportunity.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Below-Zone (Below the Promotion Zone). Below-Zone officers are junior to the junior officer in the promotion zone (In-Zone). Below-Zone officers are eligible for consideration, but if not selected, they will not incur a failure of selection. The number of Below-Zone officers authorized to be selected may not exceed 10 percent of the total number of officers the PSB is authorized to recommend for promotion; however, where the number authorized by this calculation would be less than one, the board may recommend one Below- Zone officer. Additionally, the Below-Zone population is generally a rough estimate of the following year's In-Zone population. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 1-11 Enclosure (2)

provision.text: Remove. An officer whose name is removed from a promotion list per section 629 of reference (a) incurs a failure of selection (unless selected from the below zone) and continues to be eligible for consideration for promotion. If the officer is recommended for promotion by the next selection board, and the SECNAV approves the report of the board, the officer's name shall be placed on the promotion list without prejudice. Per sections 629 and 14501 of reference (a), an officer once removed is considered for all purposes as having twice failed of selection for promotion to the next higher grade upon the following: the officer is not recommended for promotion in the approved report of the next selection board; the officer is so recommended, but the President, or the SECNAV acting for the President, removes the officer's name from the promotion list; or if the Senate rejects the officer's appointment. 5004. PROMOTION BOARD SCHEDULE. Officer promotion boards are based on a fiscal year schedule. In the second quarter of each fiscal year, the CMC (MMPR-1) will publish the board schedule, via MARADMIN, for the succeeding fiscal year. In addition to the board convening dates, this message will contain information on reviewing and updating an officer’s Official Military Personnel File (OMPF) and other administrative instructions that are applicable to all promotion boards. 2001. NOTICE OF CONVENING. Sections 614 and 14105 of reference (a) require that, at least 30 days prior to the date the board is convened, the CMC (MMPR- 1) must provide general written notice to eligible officers. This shall be accomplished through a standard naval message (MARADMIN), and at a minimum will include:

provision.label: a.
provision.text: The name and date of the junior eligible officer in the below-zone as of the date of the notice.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Submission of update material to the board.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Submission of Reserve Qualification Summaries (RQS) to Reserve selection boards.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Auditing and correcting Official Military Personnel Files (OMPF), see MCO P1610.7A.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Implementation of any unique regulation such as the 90-day rule or continuation in an active status. 2002. BOARD COMPOSITION

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Open-source information not contained in the OMPF, such as school and command screening messages. Any information that is not part of an officer's OMPF is strictly prohibited.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Current separation or retirement status, unless provided by the eligible officer as update material sent to the President of the board.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Current medical status, unless provided by the eligible officer as update material sent to the President of the board. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 3-4 Enclosure (2)

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Any information received from third parties not endorsed or forwarded by the eligible officer.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Any information regarding an action that was completed after the date the board convened (e.g. awards certificates, fitness reports, disciplinary actions, etc.). 3002. REQUEST FOR NON-SELECTION. Some eligible officers on the active-duty list may intend to leave active duty and therefore submit a written request not to be selected for promotion to the board president. Any officer In or Above-Zone who submits a request for non-selection will still be considered by the board, but will incur a failure of selection if not recommended for promotion by the board. Per section 1174 of reference (a), an officer discharged for twice failing of selection is not entitled to separation pay if either (or both) of those failures of selection was the action of a selection board to which the officer submitted a request in writing not to be selected for promotion or who otherwise directly caused his/her own non-selection through written communication to the board. Accordingly, selection boards convened under sections 611a of reference (a) are required to include in the board report the names of those officers who fall into this category. All requests for non-selection must be received within ten calendar days of the board convene date per 10 U.S.C. section 614. 3003. RESERVE QUALIFICATION SUMMARY (RQS). Reserve officers (except AR officers) are required to submit an RQS to selection boards for which they are eligible. This document provides valuable information regarding the officer's activities when not actively participating in the Reserve Marine Corps. Additional information pertaining to the RQS requirement is outlined in the annual Board Schedule MARADMIN. 3004. ASSIGNMENT OF CASES. Assignment of eligible officers' cases to each board member is accomplished randomly by computer amongst the board members. Board presidents will be assigned half the number of cases as other board members to account for the additional administrative duties associated with their position. 3005. CASE PREPARATION AND BRIEFING. The officer selection process is composed of four phases, thus ensuring each officer's record is thoroughly reviewed, briefed, considered, and voted on by the selection board.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: outlines the preparation procedures and specifies what documents must be contained in the nomination package. 4007. BOARD APPROVAL PROCESS. Once the members of a board sign the board report and the CMC (MMPR-1) has prepared the nomination package, both packages are forwarded to the final approval authority. All selection boards must be endorsed, first by the Commandant of the Marine Corps, and second by the Office of the Judge Advocate General of the Navy, before being forwarded to the SECNAV. Figure 4-1 contains a detailed chart, which indicates the offices the board report, and, when applicable, the nomination package must be routed through prior to release of the results and ultimate board approval authority. 4008. NOTIFICATION OF BOARD RESULTS
You are entitled to submit matters for consideration in response to the promotion delay.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Promote. If the decision is that the officer should be promoted, the officer will receive the original date of rank he/she would have had if no such delay had occurred; however, per reference (a), sections 624 and 14311, the SECNAV has the authority to adjust the date of rank of an officer if the Secretary believes the officer was unqualified for promotion during any part of the period of delay. For second lieutenants promoted to first lieutenant, and warrant officers promoted to chief warrant officer 2, date of rank adjustment authority rests with the Commandant of the Marine Corps.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Remove. Removal decision actions for promotion delays are the same as for promotion withholds (see paragraph 5003.2.b). 5005. ELIGIBILITY IMPLICATIONS. While an officer is in a withhold or a delay status, he/she is not eligible for any subsequent promotion boards. Sections 619 and 14301 of reference (a) preclude from consideration an officer whose name is on a promotion list for that grade as a result of selection at a previous promotion board (or eligibility for promotion as a result of achieving time in grade requirements). 5006. SPECIAL SELECTION BOARDS (SSBs) AND SPECIAL SELECTION REVIEW BOARDS (SSRBs). Post-board screening for officers selected for promotion by an SSB or SSRB is conducted in accordance with the procedures outlined in paragraph 5002 and 5003. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 5-5 Enclosure (2) 5007. SECOND LIEUTENANTS (O-1). All second lieutenants appointed during a calendar year are screened for qualifications for promotion to first lieutenant and their names are forwarded to the Secretary of Defense for approval prior to appointment to first lieutenant. Officers with adverse material will follow the same procedures listed above with regard to the opportunity to comment and subsequent qualification for promotion decision. 5008. WARRANT OFFICERS (W-1). All W-1s appointed during a calendar year are screened for qualification for promotion to chief warrant officer 2 and their names are forwarded to the Secretary of Defense for approval prior to appointment to chief warrant officer 2 (CWO2). Officers with adverse material will follow the same procedures listed above with regard to the opportunity to comment and subsequent qualification for promotion decision. and any statements you wish to submit should be addressed, via your chain of command, to the Commandant of the Marine Corps (JPL), Headquarters, U.S. Marine Corps, 3000 Marine Corps Pentagon, Washington, DC 20350-3000. Any statement or information you wish to provide must be submitted within 10 days of receipt of this letter.
Per sections 578, 626, and 14309 of reference (a), no oath is required if the officer has served continuously since the officer originally accepted his/her commission.

If the officer has not served continuously, the officer is required to take the oath of commissioning as follows: "I (state your full name) do solemnly swear (or affirm) that I will support and defend the Constitution of the United States against all enemies, foreign and domestic; that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the same; that I take this obligation freely, without any mental reservation or purpose of evasion; and that I will well and faithfully discharge the duties of the office on which I am about to enter. So help me God." 6007. PROMOTION CEREMONIES

There is no formal ceremonial process associated with an officer’s promotion; however, typical promotion ceremonies have evolved through MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 6-4 Enclosure (2) tradition and practice. A standard officer promotion ceremony may be conducted in the following manner:

provision.label: a.
provision.text: The commission (promotion warrant) is read. A constructive promotion warrant may be read in the event the original promotion warrant has not been received.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: The officer reaffirms the oath (see paragraph 6006) from the presiding official.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Presiding officials should be senior to the officer being promoted.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: The officer’s new rank insignia is pinned on by individuals of the officer’s choosing.
Per paragraphs 6001, the commission is not the legal authority to promote.
Under no circumstances will an officer be promoted prior to the effective date, regardless of what day of the week the effective date should happen to fall. 6008. FROCKING

Background. Frocking is defined as the administrative authority from SECDEF (O7 and above) or SECNAV (O6 and below) granting officers selected for promotion and, if required, confirmed by the U.S. Senate but not yet promoted, the right to wear the insignia and uniform and assume the title of the next higher grade. The Marine Corps may frock an officer per the references provided they meet one of the criteria listed in paragraph 6008.3.

Responsibility. The Officer Assignments Branch (CMC, MMOA-3) is responsible for the management and disposition of all active component officer frocking requests, except general officers. In accordance with reference (l), CMC (MMOA) must submit semiannual frocking reports to Office of the SECDEF. Reserve Affairs (CMC, RAM) is responsible for the management and disposition of all reserve component frocking requests. The Senior Leaders Management Branch (CMC, MMSL) is responsible for the management and disposition of both active and reserve component general officer frocking requests.

Eligibility. All officers shall either be serving, or have permanent change of station orders to serve, in a higher grade position and already have detached from the previous position; additionally, officers with PCS orders shall begin serving in the position of the higher grade within 60 days of the requested frocking date. If extended delays in reporting are expected during PCS, CMC may frock officers in grades O-8 and below for no more than 120 days before they begin serving in the higher grade position. In this case, frocking may occur no earlier than the date that an officer detaches from the previous duty station. In addition, requests for frocking must meet at least one of the criteria below without exception.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Billets with the title of Defense Attaché, Marine Attaché or Naval Attaché.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Billets attached to the immediate staffs of the Offices of the President and Vice President of the United States. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 6-5 Enclosure (2)

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Joint Duty Assignments List (JDAL) billets JD1 or JD2 coded billets.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Select Service Headquarters billets including, but not limited to, billets attached to immediate staffs of the Service Secretaries, Service Under Secretaries and Assistant Service Secretaries as defined in sections 3014 b(1) & (2), 5014 b(1) & (2), & 8014 b(1) & (2) of reference (a).

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Billets with the title Commanding Officer (CO).

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Billets with the title Executive Officer (XO).

provision.label: g.
provision.text: Acquisition Corps major program manager billets (ACAT I).
Not Eligible for Frocking

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Officers who elect not to be frocked, or decline promotion.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Enlisted personnel selected for officer appointment.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Officers not confirmed by the Senate, where Senate confirmation is required by statute.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Officers who do not meet Marine Corps weight or body fat standards.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Officers being considered for removal from a promotion list or who are being considered for promotion delay.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Second Lieutenants and Warrant Officers within the grades of W-1 through CWO-5.
Limitations. Per reference (a), field grade officer frocking is limited to 1% of major and lieutenant colonel end-strength; 2% of colonel end- strength.
Guidelines. The following guidelines apply:

provision.label: a.
provision.text: DOD precedence for frocking officers to grades major through brigadier general is:
Positions in the international environment.
Joint duty positions.
Command positions.
Other unusual circumstances, as SECNAV determines.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Frocking does not authorize increased disciplinary powers under Article 15, Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ).

provision.label: c.
provision.text: A grade change (GC) fitness report is required per MCO P1610.7.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: No unit diary entry is required. MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 6-6 Enclosure (2)

provision.label: e.
provision.text: The officer will not receive any pay, allowances or entitlements to the frocked grade until the officer is actually promoted.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Commissions are not to be read at frocking ceremonies. Only the authority to frock may be read.

provision.label: g.
provision.text: Frocking requests for officers in each competitive category of the RASL shall prescribe to the same statutory limitations specified for officers on the ADL.
Authority

provision.label: a.
provision.text: General Officers. SECNAV via MMSL.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Field Grade Officers. CMC, Director, Manpower Management/Reserve Affairs (Dir, MM) for respective component.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Captains. First General Officer in the chain of command.
General Officers are authorized to frock first lieutenants to captain and chief warrant officers selected for the limited duty officer (LDO) program based on the below:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Must meet one of the criteria in paragraph 6008.3 above.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Must be serving in or within 30 days of serving in a captain's billet.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Within the criteria above, there are no restrictions on the number of captain selects the Marine Corps is authorized to frock. Officers may be frocked after the appropriate authority has approved the selection list that contains the officer's name.
Commands must notify CMC (MMOA-3) by naval message or correspondence of all officers frocked to the grade of captain and the criteria met according to 6008.3 above.
Requests. In every case, frocking must be essential to the officer's maximum effectiveness to perform the assigned duties and must clearly serve the best interest of the Marine Corps.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Requests may be submitted via naval message or naval correspondence and must contain endorsement from the chain of command. Requests must contain (figure 6-1):

Grade to which frocking is desired.
Date Time Group (DTG) of ALNAV which announced the officer's selection for promotion.
Command Name.

Billet for the higher grade to which the officer occupies, or to which the officer is ordered which may qualify for frocking. Include the title, monitored command code (MCC), and billet identification code (BIC). MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 6-7 Enclosure (2)
Requested frocking date.
Justification (must cite the specific criteria from paragraph 6008.3 above and detail description of how compliance is met).

All officers shall either be serving, or have permanent change of station orders to serve, in a higher grade position and already have detached from the previous position; additionally, officers with PCS orders shall begin serving in the position of the higher grade within 60 days of the requested frocking date. If extended delays in reporting are expected during PCS, CMC may frock officers in grades O-8 and below for no more than 120 days before they begin serving in the higher grade position. In this case, frocking may occur no earlier than the date that an officer detaches from the previous duty station. In addition, requests for frocking must meet at least one of the criteria below without exception.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Billets with the title of Defense Attaché, Marine Attaché or Naval Attaché.

provision.label: b.

provision.label: g.

COMMISSIONING OATH
Per sections 578, 626, and 14309 of reference (a), no oath is required if the officer has served continuously since the officer originally accepted his/her commission.

If the officer has not served continuously, the officer is required to take the oath of commissioning as follows: "I (state your full name) do solemnly swear (or affirm) that I will support and defend the Constitution of the United States against all enemies, foreign and domestic; that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the same; that I take this obligation freely, without any mental reservation or purpose of evasion; and that I will well and faithfully discharge the duties of the office on which I am about to enter. So help me God." 6007. PROMOTION CEREMONIES

There is no formal ceremonial process associated with an officer’s promotion; however, typical promotion ceremonies have evolved through MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 6-4 Enclosure (2) tradition and practice. A standard officer promotion ceremony may be conducted in the following manner:

provision.label: b.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Presiding officials should be senior to the officer being promoted.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: The officer’s new rank insignia is pinned on by individuals of the officer’s choosing.
Per paragraphs 6001, the commission is not the legal authority to promote.
Under no circumstances will an officer be promoted prior to the effective date, regardless of what day of the week the effective date should happen to fall. 6008. FROCKING

Background. Responsibility. The Officer Assignments Branch (CMC, MMOA-3) is responsible for the management and disposition of all active component officer frocking requests, except general officers. In accordance with reference (l), CMC (MMOA) must submit semiannual frocking reports to Office of the SECDEF. Administrative Error. Administrative error exists when an officer was eligible for consideration by a promotion selection board, but whose record was not in the eligible population viewed by that board.
Considered in an Unfair Manner. There are four subcategories in which an officer may have been considered in an unfair manner.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Board Acted Contrary to Law. The board violated statutory rules governing the conduct of promotion boards.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Material Error of Fact. There was material information in the officer’s record that was erroneous and should not have been considered by the board.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Material Administrative Error. There was a material error in the administrative functioning of the board.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Absence of Material Information. There was material information missing from the officer’s record. 7003. REQUESTING AN SSB. Per SECNAVINST 1402.1, all applications for special selection boards under paragraph 7002.2 must be received no later than three years after the date the contested board results were made public. Applications received more than three years after the date the contested board results were made public will be treated as untimely and will be denied.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Is fully qualified when compared to the selected officers whose sample records were considered; and MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 7-4 Enclosure (2)

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Is better qualified for promotion than all of the officers who failed to be selected for promotion before the regularly scheduled promotion selection board; and

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Is comparable to those officers who were selected for promotion by the regularly scheduled promotion selection board.

Administrative Error. The SECNAV shall, upon determination that an administrative error occurred, convene a SSB to consider the record of the officer concerned. Normally, the CMC (MMPR-1) will identify administrative errors; however, officers who believe they were not appropriately considered should contact CMC (MMPR-1). Upon verification of the error, CMC (MMPR-1) will notify the eligible officer. The officer must acknowledge notification of eligibility in writing. Figure 7-1 is a sample acknowledgment letter.

Considered in an Unfair Manner. The SECNAV is the approval authority for requests under this category. An officer must have been considered by a regularly scheduled selection board, and not selected. In the request, the officer must detail the circumstances in which the unfair treatment existed. Further, in cases where an officer is applying under “Material Error of Fact” or “Absence of Material Information,” additional justification will be required. Because officers are personally responsible for their own record in accordance with reference (q), officers must include a detailed account of the actions they took to promptly identify and correct the problem prior to the convening of the promotion board that did not select them. It is critical MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 7-3 Enclosure (2) that the request explain, in detail, how the officer demonstrated reasonable diligence in identifying and correcting the error that caused the failure of selection prior to the board's convening. "Reasonable diligence" is defined as fair, proper, and due degree of care and activity, measured with reference to the particular circumstances; such diligence, care and attention as might be expected from a man/woman of ordinary prudence and activity. Requests which fail to show the officer demonstrated reasonable diligence to identify and correct the error prior to the promotion board will not normally be approved by the SECNAV. Figure 7-2 is a sample request for an SSB in this category.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Board Acted Contrary to Law. The board violated statutory rules governing the conduct of promotion boards.

Per SECNAVINST 1402.1, in cases where an error existed spanning multiple promotion boards, the officer shall normally request an SSB for the earliest board where the error existed, unless the officer specifies the particular board for which relief is sought. Requests of this type must indicate the circumstances that make relief at a subsequent board more appropriate.

Promotions. An officer selected by a SSB shall, upon approval by appropriate authority (see figure 4-1) and with Senate confirmation, if applicable, have the same date of rank, the same effective date for pay and MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 7-5 Enclosure (2) allowances of that officer's grade, and the same position on the active-duty list or Reserve active-status list as the officer would have had if the officer had been recommended for promotion by the petitioned selection board. This is accomplished by release of a naval message and a unit diary entry into the Marine Corps Total Force System (MCTFS). The promotion procedures outlined in paragraphs 6002- 6004 of this Manual pertain to effecting and accepting of an SSB promotion.

Senate Confirmation. Per Chapter 4 of this Order, active duty officers who are considered for promotion by an SSB and selected by the board for the grade of major or above, and Reserve colonel or above, may not be promoted or frocked until confirmed by the Senate.

Failure of Selection. An officer who was not considered for promotion by a regularly scheduled selection board (administrative error) and is not recommended for promotion by the SSB shall be considered to have failed of selection for promotion to the next higher grade; however, an officer who fails of selection by a regularly scheduled selection board because the board considered the officer in an unfair manner, and is not recommended for promotion by a special selection board, will not incur an additional failure of selection. 7008. SPECIAL SELECTION REVIEW BOARDS (SSRB)

Section 505 of the FY21 NDAA, added sections 628(a) and 14502(a) to reference (a) that requires the Secretary of the Military Department concerned to convene a SSRB to consider credible information of an adverse nature, including any substantiated adverse finding or conclusion, that was not furnished to a PSB convened under reference (a), sections 611(a) and 14101(a).

Any SSRB convened, whether for a regular or reserve officer, to a grade at or below the grade of major general, will, to the greatest extent practicable, apply the same standards used by the PSB that originally recommended the officer for promotion and would consider the record of the officer as presented to the original PSB, along with the newly adjudicated adverse information. The SSRB would be conducted so as not to indicate or disclose the officer or officers, for whom the board is convened, as statute prohibits any affirmative action to label/identify the record for whom the SSRB is convened. The members of the SSRB are to apply a competitive process to determine whether or not to sustain the original promotion recommendation of the officer or officers, at issue. An officer whose promotion is recommended for sustainment by a SSRB would be appointed, pending the review and confirmation process, to the next higher grade, as soon as the Record of Proceedings (ROP) is approved, and, upon appointment, would have the same date of rank as the officer would have had pursuant to the recommendation of the original PSB. If a SSRB did not sustain a recommendation for promotion of an officer, that officer would be considered to have failed selection for promotion.
The SSRB process is as follows:

provision.label: a.
provision.text: For timeline purposes, upon completion of any investigation and related action, Judge Advocate Division will notify the officer that their case is closed, be it through the officer disciplinary notebook or Inspector General, and provide the officer an opportunity to submit matters (section five of this Order). The Commandant of the Marine Corps, after review of the MCO 1400.31D 28 Oct 2021 7-6 Enclosure (2) officer’s matters, will than recommend the officer be removed from the list or make a request, to SECNAV, to convene a SSRB. If a SSRB is directed, MMPR-1 will notify the officer and provide the officer 30 days to respond. Such notice will include a copy of the adverse information summary, if the adverse material is not already in the officer’s OMPF. After the thirty day response time period, members are appointed for the SSRB and the precept is routed for SECNAV approval. At that point, the SSRB can convene and, after adjournment, the ROP is forwarded through the Commandant of the Marine Corps (CMC), the SECNAV, the Secretary of Defense (SECDEF), and then to the President and Senate, as appropriate.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: The name of any officer recommended for promotion, who is subject to review by a SSRB, shall not be disseminated or publicly released on the list of officers recommended for promotion, and shall not be forwarded to the SECDEF, the President, or the Senate, as applicable, until the SSRB has made its recommendation.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: In considering any officer recommended for promotion, and whether the recommendation for promotion of the officer should be sustained, a SSRB shall be furnished, and consider, the record and information concerning the officer furnished to the PSB that recommended the officer for promotion, to include any credible information of an adverse nature on said officer,. However, before the adverse information is furnished to the SSRB, SECNAV (or his or her designee) shall ensure that the information is made available to the officer and that said officer is afforded a reasonable opportunity to submit comments on such information to the SSRB, usually thirty days.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: The SSRB shall compare the officer’s record, including adverse information, with an appropriate sampling of the records of those officers of the same competitive category who were recommended for promotion by the PSB that recommended the officer for promotion, and an appropriate sampling of the records of those officers who were considered by, and not recommended for, promotion by that PSB. As noted previously, the records and information shall be presented to a SSRB in a manner that does not indicate or disclose the officer for whom the SSRB was convened.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: The recommendation for promotion of an officer may be sustained only if the SSRB determines that said officer is more competitive than the non-select sample records said officer is comparable to the select sample records. A recommendation for promotion is only sustained by a vote of a majority of the members of the SSRB. If a SSRB does not sustain a recommendation for promotion of an officer under this section, the officer shall be considered to have failed of selection for promotion. provision.label: a.

provision.label: c.

Any update material provided to the SSB cannot contain information about or refer to events that took place after the convening date of the petitioned board. Any update material must be received prior to ten calendar days before the board. 7005. SAMPLING OF RECORDS. Pursuant to reference (q) and per paragraph 4003, all regularly scheduled promotion selection boards identify a sampling of records of the eligible population that are retained for each grade and competitive category. The eligible officer's record will be compared against these records per paragraph 7004. 7006. BOARD ACTIONS

Number Authorized to Select. The prescribed number to select is not subject to the promotion percentage limitations ordinarily imposed upon regular selection boards. Specific guidance for each board is contained in the SSB’s precept.
Selection Standard. Per sections 628 and 14502 of reference (a), an eligible officer’s record will be compared against the sampling of records, and the following selection criteria will be applied:

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Board Acted Contrary to Law. The board violated statutory rules governing the conduct of promotion boards.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Material Error of Fact. There was material information in the officer’s record that was erroneous and should not have been considered by the board.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Material Administrative Error. There was a material error in the administrative functioning of the board.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Absence of Material Information. There was material information missing from the officer’s record. 7003. REQUESTING AN SSB. Per SECNAVINST 1402.1, all applications for special selection boards under paragraph 7002.2 must be received no later than three years after the date the contested board results were made public. Applications received more than three years after the date the contested board results were made public will be treated as untimely and will be denied.

provision.label: b.

provision.label: c.
